subject: Climate Activism at Roosevelt Circle
overview: Medford Bytes host Danielle Balocca spoke with musician and activist Warren Senders about his weekday climate vigils at Roosevelt Circle. Senders discussed how daily discipline, Hindustani singing, and long-term thinking intersect with his environmental and political advocacy.

items.title: Introduction and Medford Favorites
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduced musician and activist Warren Senders, who shared his favorite Medford eateries.

items.title: Origins of the Daily Roadside Vigil
items.summary: Senders explained his daily weekday climate vigils at Roosevelt Circle, which began in 2015 and combine sign displays with his practice of Hindustani Khayal singing following an earlier four-year daily letter-writing effort.

items.title: Sign Messages and Community Responses
items.summary: Senders described the rotating messages on his signs emphasizing long-term thinking and urgent action, alongside the range of supportive and hostile reactions from passing drivers.

items.title: Perspectives on Activism, Politics, and Culture
items.summary: Senders detailed his framework distinguishing unyielding activism from political compromise, emphasizing the role of cultural and musical traditions in sustaining long-term human connection.

items.title: Musical Performance and Vigil Invitation
items.summary: Senders performed a vocal composition set to a quote by Isaac Newton and invited listeners to join his weekday morning vigils at Roosevelt Circle.
